title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 124
paragraphs: Although the Greeks, out of envy, would give no decision on this but sailed off each to his own city without reaching a verdict, Themistocles was nevertheless loudly talked about and esteemed throughout Greece as by far the ablest of the Greeks. Since he had received no honor from those who had fought at Salamis, even though he was first in the voting, he at once went on to Lacedaemon, wishing to receive honor there. The Lacedaemonians received him well and gave him great honors. As a prize of valor they gave Eurybiades a wreath of olive; and for ability and skill they gave Themistocles too a wreath of olive, and presented him besides with the chariot judged the best in Sparta. Having praised him highly, they escorted him on his departure with three hundred picked Spartans — those called the “Horsemen” — as far as the borders of Tegea. He is the only man we know of to whom the Spartans ever gave an escort on his way.
